evals.name: target-and-compiler-internals
evals.prompt: We build Java on a newer JDK for older runtimes. Only source/target is set. Add Error Prone and formatting while keeping existing processors and test JVM agents.
expectations: Sets an explicit release/API target and verifies a newer platform API is rejected.
Checks current stable Error Prone and formatter compatibility with actual compiler JDK.
Distinguishes in-process build JVM access from forked javac JVM flags.
Preserves annotation processor paths and delegates test JVM agent wiring to the build integration.
Pins tool versions only in the consuming project.

evals.name: formatter-style-conflict
evals.prompt: After the formatter runs, our full Checkstyle preset rejects output and test sources are not checked. Fix the configuration without excluding every test.
expectations: Keeps one formatter and reconciles contradictory Checkstyle rules with clear ownership.
Includes applicable Java production and test sources.
Checks effective severity/failure behavior as well as failOnViolation.
Proves formatter output passes style checks and verify does not mutate files.

evals.name: analyzer-overlap
evals.prompt: Set up Java correctness/security analysis for a mixed Java/Kotlin reactor. Proposed tools are Error Prone, SpotBugs/FindSecBugs and every PMD/CPD rule.
expectations: Curates complementary rule ownership rather than enabling every rule or duplicate concern.
Verifies failing check goals rather than reports alone.
Confines Java source rules to Java sources and reviews Kotlin bytecode signal deliberately.
Uses narrow justified suppressions and preserves existing compatible choices.

evals.name: feature-work-boundary
evals.prompt: Fix one Java behavior bug in a legacy repo with pinned tools and accepted generated-source exclusions. The current build has an unrelated baseline finding.
expectations: Keeps feature work focused and does not silently upgrade tools or reformat the repository.
Adds meaningful tests and reports remaining gate failures honestly.
Does not lower thresholds, regenerate baselines or widen exclusions just to pass.
Uses the configured verification command and exact project pins.

evals.name: immutable-shipment-snapshot
evals.prompt: Implement Java 17 ShipmentSnapshot (default package), a value snapshot with public constructor ShipmentSnapshot(String id, List<Parcel> parcels, byte[] label) and accessors String id(), List<Parcel> parcels(), byte[] label(). Parcel is an existing mutable collaborator: constructor Parcel(String sku, int quantity), getters sku()/quantity(), setters setSku(String)/setQuantity(int). You may not change Parcel or these signatures. Preserve parcel order and duplicates; empty parcels is valid. Reject null/blank id, null collection/label, null elements, and parcels with null/blank SKU or nonpositive quantity. The instance must remain the same shipment after construction. Provide ShipmentSnapshot.java and concise notes.md; no build changes.
expectations: Owns the input collection, every mutable Parcel element, and label array rather than relying only on final fields or a record.
Prevents accessor mutations (including nested Parcel setters and array changes) from modifying retained shipment state.
Validates the retained snapshot, preserves order/duplicates and allows an empty parcel list.
Uses a small compatible API; does not require a builder or change the existing Parcel class.

evals.name: legacy-date-range
evals.prompt: Implement Java 17 DateRange with public DateRange(java.util.Date start, java.util.Date end), start()/end() returning Date, and long durationMillis(). This public legacy signature must remain. Dates may be Date subtypes. Require nonnull dates and end >= start; equal endpoints are valid. The range is a stable value independent of later caller activity. Supply DateRange.java and notes.md. Do not change public signatures or add libraries.
expectations: Creates trusted owned values/copies from mutable inputs without trusting subtype clone implementations.
Checks ordering on the retained values rather than validating original dates and copying afterward.
Prevents mutable accessor results from exposing internal state and preserves the legacy signatures.
Explains ownership assumptions without claiming an atomic snapshot of arbitrary concurrently modified inputs.

evals.name: failure-atomic-stock-ledger
evals.prompt: Implement Java 17 StockLedger with constructor StockLedger(Map<String,Integer> initial), void reserve(Map<String,Integer> request), and Map<String,Integer> stock(). This is intentionally mutable, single-owner, single-threaded state: reserve deducts requested counts in place. Initial entries require nonblank keys and nonnegative counts. Requests require known nonblank keys and strictly positive counts no larger than available stock. Null maps, null keys and null counts are invalid. Empty requests are valid. Any rejected request must leave every count unchanged. stock() returns a read-only snapshot at call time. Supply StockLedger.java and notes.md; preserve signatures and use standard Java only.
expectations: Validates/snapshots the complete request and prepares changes before publishing deductions, avoiding partial mutation on rejection.
Owns constructor map state and returns stable read-only snapshots rather than backed views.
Handles required invalid inputs, empty batches and ordinary valid in-place reservations.
Keeps purposeful mutation and avoids an unauthorized immutable API redesign or unnecessary copying of immutable Integer/String values.

evals.name: counting-set-composition
evals.prompt: Implement Java 17 public CountingSet<E> usable as a Set<E>, with a no-arg constructor and long totalAdded(). totalAdded is the lifetime count of successful element insertions: duplicate adds do not increment it; removing and re-adding an element increments again. addAll must count exactly the successful insertions. Preserve ordinary Set operations including iterator.remove and clear. Default HashSet null behavior is acceptable. Supply CountingSet.java and notes.md, using standard Java only.
expectations: Uses composition/delegation for storage rather than inheriting HashSet implementation behavior.
Counts bulk inserts exactly once, including duplicates and subsequent removal/reinsertion.
Preserves the Set contract, iterator removal and meaningful standard abstract extension points.
Avoids double-counting inherited self-calls and does not turn intentional mutable collection state into an immutable API.

evals.name: money-value-contracts
expectations: Provides consistent scale-insensitive value equality/hashCode and ordering including currency; verifies hash-collection use.
Uses exact BigDecimal/integer operations rather than a double round trip and rejects cross-currency arithmetic.
Establishes constructor invariants without forbidding negative amounts or changing the public record components.
Shares immutable BigDecimal/String values as appropriate instead of indiscriminate defensive copying.

evals.name: api-review-with-mutation-control
expectations: Identifies shared mutable state/order hazards in the parallel stream and swallowed IOException; proposes observable ordered writes.
Validates the whole input before effects and records a row only after a completed write.
Preserves borrowed-resource ownership, the intentional live view and purposeful mutation; does not prescribe closing the Writer or forcing immutable service state.
Distinguishes local state guarantees from external partial output; does not claim copying creates a transactional Writer.
